thrill.definition: One of the three emotions. Shown as a blue lightning bolt icon on concession tiles, attraction cards and property spaces. Each Thrill icon earned advances your emotion disc one space to the right on the Thrill track. The Thrill track is the first track evaluated during the Bonuses step.

awe.definition: One of the three emotions. Shown as a yellow star icon. Each Awe icon earned advances your emotion disc one space to the right on the Awe track. The Awe track is the second track evaluated during the Bonuses step, and its bonus can hand you the shovel token.

joy.definition: One of the three emotions. Shown as a red heart icon. Each Joy icon earned advances your emotion disc one space to the right on the Joy track. The Joy track is the third and last track evaluated during the Bonuses step.

emotion_track.definition: One of the three tracks on the game board (Thrill, Awe, Joy) along which players move their emotion discs. Discs move one space to the right for each matching emotion icon earned. A disc that would move past the end of a track is instead placed on top of all other discs on the final space. Each disc that ends the game above the eighth space of a track scores 5 VP.

emotion_disc.definition: A round marker in your player color. Each player has three, one on each emotion track. Discs stack: a disc moved onto an occupied space goes on top of the discs already there, and the disc on top counts as farthest along when players share a space. Discs left behind keep their existing order.

property.definition: Your personal play area: your property board plus any expansion boards you have added to it. All concession tiles and attraction tiles must be placed on your property following the tile placement rules.

property_board.definition: The double-sided board each player takes during setup, placed with either side face up. It is covered in a grid of spaces, some showing tree spaces (which start with a tree marker) and some showing emotion, money or wild icons that are triggered when a tile covers them. The front of each board is identical; the back has a unique arrangement of tree spaces and icons.

expansion_board.definition: A small double-sided board bought with the Realtor action for $3. It is placed aligned to the far-left or far-right side of your existing property, either side face up, and a tree marker is added to each of its indicated tree spaces. It then counts as part of your property. There is no limit to how many you may add.

concession_tile.definition: A small tile taken with the Contractor action from the face-up supply and placed on your property. Concession tiles show emotion icons (advancing your discs when built) and may show income, which pays out every Income step. Face-up tiles are cleared and re-revealed each Cleanup step.

attraction_tile.definition: The physical tile matching an attraction card. When you take the Builder action you place the matching attraction tile on your property following the tile placement rules. Tiles are double-sided and may be rotated to any orientation and placed with either side up.

attraction_card.definition: A card bought with the Builder action. It shows the build cost, the emotion icons gained when its tile is built, an advertising cost, VP for advertising, sometimes income, and the VP it is worth at game end. Once bought, the card is flipped face down in front of you; it still pays income and can still be advertised.

attraction_type.definition: The six themed types of attraction, identified by banner color and icon: Souvenir, Old West, Sci-Fi, Undersea, Fantasy and Prehistoric. Each type has its own face-up card stack around the central opening of the board, and each stack is aligned with one Builder location and one carousel ring cost modifier.

carousel.definition: The three-dimensional centerpiece assembled before the first game and set inside the round opening of the game board, resting in the carousel ring.

carousel_ring.definition: The ring the carousel sits in. Each of its segments shows a cost modifier that applies to the attraction card stack it is aligned with, raising or lowering the Builder cost. It starts with +$2 aligned to the Souvenir stack, and the player with the shovel token rotates it during every Cleanup step; the position must change.

worker.definition: Your placement pieces; each player has three. During the Actions step you place one worker at a time on an action space and immediately take that action. All workers return to their owners during Cleanup.

extra_action_worker.definition: The single tan worker kept on its designated space on the game board. The player farthest along the Thrill track may take it during the Bonuses step (by moving their Thrill disc back one space) to place a fourth worker during the next month's Actions step. Taking the 1 VP option on the Thrill track instead returns it to the board.

shovel_token.definition: The start player marker. It is given at setup to the player who most recently rode a roller coaster. Its holder starts the Actions step and rotates the carousel ring during Cleanup. It changes hands via the Awe track bonus in the Bonuses step.

tree_marker.definition: A green tree that blocks a space on your property. Trees start on the indicated tree spaces of your property board and are added to each indicated tree space of any expansion board you take. Tiles may not overlap a tree marker (though they may share a side with one). The Arborist action removes up to two trees from your property.

wild_icon.definition: An icon on a property or expansion board space. For each wild icon a newly placed tile covers, advance one space on any emotion track of your choice.

money.definition: Currency, in $1 and $3 tokens. Gained during the Income step ($3 plus income icons), from the Banker action ($2), from the Joy track bonus ($3), and by covering $2 or $4 icons on your property. Spent to build attractions, to advertise, and for the Realtor action ($3). Money is also the first tiebreaker at game end.

income.definition: The recurring money shown on some built concession tiles and attraction cards. During the Income step each player takes $3 from the supply plus the income shown on all of their built concessions and attractions.

advertising.definition: During the Advertising step, a player may pay the advertising cost printed on one of their attraction cards to immediately take the number of VP tokens shown. Each attraction may be advertised once per month.

visiting_people.definition: The victory point tokens, in 1-VP and 5-VP denominations. VP are gained from emotion track bonuses, advertising, goal cards, attraction card values, emotion discs finishing above the eighth space, and the attraction count bonus. The player with the most VP at the end of the fifth month wins.

goal_card.definition: A secret end-game objective. Each player is dealt three during setup, keeps two, and returns the third to the box. Each goal satisfied at the end of the game is worth 3 VP.

month.definition: A round. The game lasts five months, tracked by the month marker. Each month runs through five steps in order: Income, Actions, Bonuses, Advertising, Cleanup.

becky.definition: The virtual opponent in a solo game. She takes simplified actions, builds attractions and gains VP tokens as a human player would, but never gains or spends money. She uses no property board and no goal cards. You win by finishing with more VP tokens than Becky.
